From 859380694f434597407632c29f30fdb5e763e6cc Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jianbo Liu <jianbol@nvidia.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 13:46:52 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net/mlx5e: Fix "scheduling while atomic" in IPsec MAC address
 query

Fix a "scheduling while atomic" bug in mlx5e_ipsec_init_macs() by
replacing mlx5_query_mac_address() with ether_addr_copy() to get the
local MAC address directly from netdev->dev_addr.

The issue occurs because mlx5_query_mac_address() queries the hardware
which involves mlx5_cmd_exec() that can sleep, but it is called from
the mlx5e_ipsec_handle_event workqueue which runs in atomic context.

The MAC address is already available in netdev->dev_addr, so no need
to query hardware. This avoids the sleeping call and resolves the bug.

Call trace:
  BUG: scheduling while atomic: kworker/u112:2/69344/0x00000200
  __schedule+0x7ab/0xa20
  schedule+0x1c/0xb0
  schedule_timeout+0x6e/0xf0
  __wait_for_common+0x91/0x1b0
  cmd_exec+0xa85/0xff0 [mlx5_core]
  mlx5_cmd_exec+0x1f/0x50 [mlx5_core]
  mlx5_query_nic_vport_mac_address+0x7b/0xd0 [mlx5_core]
  mlx5_query_mac_address+0x19/0x30 [mlx5_core]
  mlx5e_ipsec_init_macs+0xc1/0x720 [mlx5_core]
  mlx5e_ipsec_build_accel_xfrm_attrs+0x422/0x670 [mlx5_core]
  mlx5e_ipsec_handle_event+0x2b9/0x460 [mlx5_core]
  process_one_work+0x178/0x2e0
  worker_thread+0x2ea/0x430

Fixes: cee137a63431 ("net/mlx5e: Handle ESN update events")
Signed-off-by: Jianbo Liu <jianbol@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Leon Romanovsky <leonro@nvidia.com>
Signed-off-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260224114652.1787431-6-tariqt@nvidia.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ipsec.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ipsec.c
index 9c7064187ed0..f03507a522b4 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ipsec.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ipsec.c
@@ -259,7 +259,6 @@ static void mlx5e_ipsec_init_limits(struct mlx5e_ipsec_sa_entry *sa_entry,
 static void mlx5e_ipsec_init_macs(struct mlx5e_ipsec_sa_entry *sa_entry,
 				  struct mlx5_accel_esp_xfrm_attrs *attrs)
 {
-	struct mlx5_core_dev *mdev = mlx5e_ipsec_sa2dev(sa_entry);
 	struct mlx5e_ipsec_addr *addrs = &attrs->addrs;
 	struct net_device *netdev = sa_entry->dev;
 	struct xfrm_state *x = sa_entry->x;
@@ -276,7 +275,7 @@ static void mlx5e_ipsec_init_macs(struct mlx5e_ipsec_sa_entry *sa_entry,
 	    attrs->type != XFRM_DEV_OFFLOAD_PACKET)
 		return;
 
-	mlx5_query_mac_address(mdev, addr);
+	ether_addr_copy(addr, netdev->dev_addr);
 	switch (attrs->dir) {
 	case XFRM_DEV_OFFLOAD_IN:
 		src = attrs->dmac;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

This patch fixes a "scheduling while atomic" bug by eliminating a blocking hardware query (`mlx5_query_mac_address()`) in the IPsec MAC address initialization code path.

### Modifications in the file

**File:** `drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en_accel/ipsec.c`

1. **Removed** the local variable `mdev` (pointer to `mlx5_core_dev`) which was derived from `sa_entry` via `mlx5e_ipsec_sa2dev()`.
2. **Replaced** the call `mlx5_query_mac_address(mdev, addr)` with `ether_addr_copy(addr, netdev->dev_addr)`.

### Relationships between modifications

- The fix addresses a context violation: `mlx5_query_mac_address()` internally uses `mlx5_cmd_exec()` which can sleep, but the function `mlx5e_ipsec_init_macs()` is called from a workqueue running in atomic context.
- The replacement eliminates the need to query hardware by retrieving the MAC address directly from `netdev->dev_addr`, which is already available and up‑to‑date.
- The removal of the `mdev` variable is a necessary cleanup because it is no longer used after the change. This makes the code simpler and avoids any potential misuse of a sleeping API in atomic context.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
mlx5_query_mac_address(mdev, addr);
```
Reason:
This function triggers a hardware command (`mlx5_cmd_exec`) that can sleep. It is called from `mlx5e_ipsec_init_macs()`, which runs in the atomic context of the `mlx5e_ipsec_handle_event` workqueue, causing a "scheduling while atomic" BUG.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
ether_addr_copy(addr, netdev->dev_addr);
```
Reason:
The local MAC address is already stored in `netdev->dev_addr`, so a simple memory copy replaces the sleeping hardware query. This avoids the atomic context violation while providing the same information.
